title: AR Elder Dragon
tagline: Summoning League of Legends' Elder Dragon into the Bird's Nest — a moment that carried the game far beyond its players.

body: League of Legends is one of the most popular gaming IPs in the world, and Worlds 2017 at the Beijing Olympic Stadium was a chance to show its characters at a scale fans had never seen. How could we use one of the most iconic venues on earth as part of the story?

Augmented reality at this size, scope and scale had never been done. Live AR for broadcast had always meant flat graphics placed into 3D space — this needed custom character design, animation and software development.

feature.caption: The Elder Dragon, conjured in AR over the arena.

body: I pitched and led the creative ideation, development and execution of the AR Elder Dragon that flew into the stadium during the opening ceremony — working with composers, artists, choreographers and art directors to make a creature from the game feel real to fans in the stadium and the audience at home.

It was treated as R&D until we proved it possible. I brought in the partners to make it real: Zero Density as the render engine, for its unique ability to cast live shadows across 3D geometry via a port of Unreal Engine, and Passion Republic for animation and design, for their expertise in real-time character optimization.
led: Pitched and led creative ideation and execution
Sourced the technical and creative partners
Led all onsite execution and day-to-day artist feedback

impact.note: The dragon became a cultural phenomenon overnight — covered by all major news outlets, posted by LeBron James, and winning Riot Games its first-ever Emmy. It put League of Legends in front of an audience far beyond gaming, and set the standard for real-time graphics the industry still follows.
